title.narrative: Green and decent jobs for youth (WeWork) in Busoga Region

description.narrative: 1. To increase the technical knowledge and skills of 500 young people in Kamuli and Jinja in the sectors of piggery, poultry, and fish enterprises that offer the prospect of decent waged employment or self-employment by 2026 2. To increase the capacity of 500 young people in Jinja and Kamuli to transition and utilise skills acquired in piggery, poultry, and fisheries by offering post-training support/services including startup-kits, business support training, access to finance and extensions services, by 2026.

The project targets 500 vulnerable young people between the ages of 15-35 in Jinja and Kamuli districts, with an emphasis on inclusivity. The beneficiaries include both men and women (50% female participation) from marginalized communities, particularly those who face economic hardship, social exclusion, and limited access to education and employment opportunities.
Special consideration is given to persons with disabilities, teenage mothers, and young people from hard-to-reach areas. These groups often face barriers in accessing vocational training and employment due to financial constraints, gender norms, and physical limitations. To ensure their full participation, the project provides accessible training facilities, transportation support, childcare services, and customized mentorship programs.
The project also targets youth with limited formal education who are eager to acquire hands-on skills in agribusiness. These beneficiaries will undergo tailored training in piggery, poultry, and fish farming, equipping them with practical skills for both self-employment and wage employment in the three trades. By integrating them into structured business groups and linking them to financial services, the project aims to enhance their economic resilience and sustainability.

Uganda has a young population with over 75% of its citizens below the age of 30. However, youth unemployment remains a critical challenge, particularly in rural areas such as Busoga. Limited access to quality education, inadequate vocational training, and a lack of formal employment opportunities contribute to high levels of underemployment and economic vulnerability among young people.
The Busoga region, where Jinja and Kamuli districts are located, is predominantly agricultural, yet youth engagement in agribusiness is low due to skill gaps, inadequate financial support, and a lack of mentorship. While agriculture holds immense potential for economic growth, young people often struggle to access the necessary resources to establish viable farming enterprises or secure employment in agricultural value chains.
Additionally, gender disparities, disability-related barriers, and social norms further marginalize vulnerable groups, including women and persons with disabilities. Teenage mothers, for instance, face cultural and financial constraints that prevent them from participating in skills training and economic activities.
This project addresses these challenges by equipping the youth with relevant agricultural and entrepreneurial skills, fostering private-sector engagement, and providing structured support to ensure sustainable employment and business opportunities. By leveraging existing community resources and aligning with national employment strategies, through his project Cordaid aims to create a more inclusive & resilient youth workforce in Busoga.
